# bronto_monitor (Resource)

Manages a Bronto monitor. Only monitors that reference an existing metric definition (via `metric_id`) are supported - not the API's alternative form with inline queries/formulas.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bronto_metric_definition" "error_rate" {
  name = "api_error_rate"
  queries = [
    {
      name   = "errors"
      select = ["count(*)"]
      where  = "status_code >= 500"
      from   = ["41521f35-1b06-41f0-9cdc-9a938b5739d1"]
      aggregation = {
        time      = "count"
        reduce_to = "avg"
      }
    }
  ]
}

# A monitor always references an existing bronto_metric_definition by id -
# it can't embed queries/formulas of its own.
resource "bronto_monitor" "error_rate" {
  name                = "High error rate"
  description         = "Error rate is above threshold over the last 20 minutes"
  metric_id           = bronto_metric_definition.error_rate.id
  comparison_operator = "ABOVE"
  threshold           = 50
  warning_threshold   = 25
  window              = "Last 20 minutes"

  actions = [
    {
      type  = "EMAIL"
      email = "oncall@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

# An anomaly detection monitor, comparing against a trailing baseline
# instead of a fixed threshold.
resource "bronto_monitor" "error_rate_anomaly" {
  name                = "Unusual error rate"
  metric_id           = bronto_metric_definition.error_rate.id
  monitor_type        = "ANOMALY_DETECTION"
  comparison_operator = "OUTSIDE"
  threshold           = 3
  evaluation_window   = "7 days"
  window              = "Last 20 minutes"

  actions = [
    {
      type  = "EMAIL"
      email = "oncall@example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `actions` (Attributes Set) The notifications to send when the monitor fires or resolves. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions))
- `comparison_operator` (String) The comparison operator of the monitor. `OUTSIDE` is two-sided and only allowed for `ANOMALY_DETECTION` monitors.
- `metric_id` (String) The id of the `bronto_metric_definition` this monitor tracks. The monitor references it rather than owning its lifecycle - deleting the monitor does not delete the metric definition.
- `name` (String) The name of the monitor
- `threshold` (Number) The threshold the monitor compares against. For `PATTERN`, `USAGE` and `CHANGE_DETECTION` monitors this is a metric value. For `ANOMALY_DETECTION` monitors it is a count of baseline spread units instead, and must be greater than 0.
- `window` (String) The time window to evaluate the monitor, e.g. `Last 20 minutes`. Minimum five minutes, maximum one day.

### Optional

- `ai_report_enabled` (Boolean) Whether an automatic AI report is generated when the monitor triggers. Defaults to `false`.
- `ai_report_instructions` (String) Instructions for the AI on what to include in the report, e.g. check for recent deployments, verify the health of the following dependencies: ...
- `anomaly_algorithm` (String) For `ANOMALY_DETECTION` monitors only - the API rejects this field for any other `monitor_type`. How the baseline is estimated; `MEDIAN_MAD` is the only supported value.
- `aux` (String) Additional monitor configuration, as a JSON-encoded string (e.g. `jsonencode({...})`)
- `change_type` (String) For `CHANGE_DETECTION` monitors only. How the change value is calculated: `DIFFERENCE` or `PERCENTAGE`.
- `compare_to` (String) For `CHANGE_DETECTION` monitors only. How far back the comparison query runs, e.g. `2 hours ago`.
- `description` (String) Extra contextual information to add to the monitor
- `evaluation_window` (String) For `ANOMALY_DETECTION` monitors only, where it is required. The trailing period used to build the baseline, e.g. `7 days`.
- `group_retention` (Number) Remove groups with no data after this many milliseconds. Defaults to `0` (never).
- `monitor_type` (String) What the monitor compares its metric against. `PATTERN` and `USAGE` compare it to a fixed threshold, `CHANGE_DETECTION` to the same metric at an earlier time (see `compare_to` and `change_type`), and `ANOMALY_DETECTION` to a trailing baseline (see `evaluation_window` and `anomaly_algorithm`). Defaults to `PATTERN`.
- `muted_until` (Number) Epoch millis timestamp the monitor is muted until. `-1` mutes indefinitely. Omit (or `0`) for unmuted. Changed after creation via a dedicated mute/unmute call, not the monitor's own update endpoint.
- `no_data_status` (String) The status to use for a group with no data (no events matched in the time window). Defaults to `OK`.
- `notify_once` (Boolean) Notify only the groups changing the global monitor status, i.e. notifications are sent only for the first group entering `ALERT` status or for the last group resolving. Defaults to `false`.
- `warning_threshold` (Number) The warning threshold value, in the same units as `threshold`. For `ANOMALY_DETECTION` monitors it must be greater than 0 and less than `threshold`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier for the monitor
- `last_trigger_ts` (Number) Epoch millis timestamp of the last time the monitor fired.
- `monitored_groups` (Attributes List) The status of each group currently being monitored. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitored_groups))
- `status` (String) The current status of the monitor.

<a id="nestedatt--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions`

Required:

- `type` (String) The kind of action: `EMAIL` or `INTEGRATION`.

Optional:

- `email` (String) The email address to notify. Required when `type` is `EMAIL`.
- `integration_id` (String) The id of the `bronto_slack_integration` or `bronto_webhook_integration` to notify. Required when `type` is `INTEGRATION`.


<a id="nestedatt--monitored_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitored_groups`

Read-Only:

- `group_id` (String) The identifier of the group.
- `groups` (Map of String) The key/value pairs that make up this group.
- `status` (String) The status of this group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Monitors can be imported by their unique ID.
terraform import bronto_monitor.error_rate 41521f35-1b06-41f0-9cdc-9a938b5739d1
```
